# Fine-tuning objective (Eq. 5)

Eq. 5 is on p. 3:

$$L_3(\mathcal{C}) = L_2(\mathcal{C}) + \lambda * L_1(\mathcal{C}) \quad (5)$$

It combines two terms:

- **$L_2(\mathcal{C})$** is the supervised objective over the labeled dataset $\mathcal{C}$ (Eq. 4, p. 3):
  $$L_2(\mathcal{C}) = \sum_{(x,y)} \log P(y \mid x^1, \dots, x^m)$$
- **$L_1(\mathcal{C})$** is the language modeling objective from pre-training (Eq. 1, p. 3), applied here to $\mathcal{C}$:
  $$L_1 = \sum_i \log P(u_i \mid u_{i-k}, \dots, u_{i-1}; \Theta)$$
  Here $k$ is the context window size.
- **$\lambda$** weights the auxiliary language modeling term (p. 3). It was set to 0.5 (Section 4.1, p. 4).

The authors say the auxiliary language modeling term helped in two ways: it improved generalization and it sped up convergence (p. 3).

**Caveat:** The document says its equations were read from the page image by a model and "can be wrong in a symbol or an index." Check the PDF before quoting this equation.
